llm.summary: The SKILL.md is mostly a documentation-only installer for a plausible security plugin, but there are a few inconsistencies and cloud-account behaviors you should verify before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (runtime security guard) matches the instructions (install OpenGuardrails plugin, restart gateway, activate). Requiring installation of an OpenClaw plugin and a registration step is reasonable for a runtime guard. Minor mismatch: registry metadata shows 'Source: unknown' and no homepage, while SKILL.md points to a GitHub repo and an npm package — you should confirm the registry package actually maps to that upstream repo/author before trusting it.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are focused on installing and activating the plugin; they do not tell the agent to read arbitrary local files or exfiltrate secrets. However, the SKILL.md contains claims about 'no install-time network calls' and 'local-only mode' that are ambiguous: the documented install step (openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/openclaw-security) will typically fetch a package from a registry (network). Also the activation flow creates an agent ID and API key on the vendor side — the registration/activation step therefore involves network activity and credential creation. These behaviors are in-scope for the plugin but worth double-checking.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill itself has no install spec or code (instruction-only), but it instructs the user to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/openclaw-security', which will pull a package (likely from npm). This is an expected install path for a plugin, but it is a network download; verify the npm package integrity and that it matches the upstream GitHub source before installing. The SKILL.md's claim 'No install-time network calls' appears inconsistent unless it means 'the plugin code does not phone home during its own local initialization.'
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or local config paths, which is appropriate for documentation-only content. However, the plugin's activation flow will create and store an API key and agent ID on the vendor side for billing/registration; sanitized metadata may be sent to a cloud assessment API if you opt in. Make sure you are comfortable with account/API-key creation and the documented minimal data that will be transmitted (name/description, usage counts, sanitized tool metadata).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request elevated platform privileges. It is installation documentation only and does not itself persist configuration. The real plugin (when installed) will persist an account/API key in the vendor system for billing — this is expected but is a persistent cloud-side artifact you should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL.md is an install/activation guide for a security plugin and is instruction-only, but before installing you should: 1) verify the npm package '@openguardrails/openclaw-security' and the GitHub repo (github.com/openguardrails/openguardrails) truly match and are maintained by the claimed author; 2) inspect the package contents (or review the repo) to confirm the local-vs-cloud behavior and that sanitization is implemented as described; 3) be aware activation will register an account and create an API key (used for billing/cloud assessments) and will involve network traffic; 4) prefer installing in a sandbox or reviewing package hashes/signatures if you do not trust the source metadata in the registry. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a provenance link (commit/tag → npm tarball hash) before installing.
